entry.title: GCP-2026-090
entry.content:
Published: 2026-11-20

Description

Description Severity Notes

2026-11-23 Update: Added details on patched PHP versions on App Engine, Cloud Run, and Cloud Run functions and noted additional details on CVEs addressed by the updated PHP versions.

A critical vulnerability was discovered in PHP's default file-based session handler. This impacts the following PHP versions:

  • PHP 8.5 < 8.5.13
  • PHP 8.4 < 8.4.28
  • PHP 8.3 < 8.3.37
  • PHP 8.2 < 8.2.36
  • PHP 8.1, PHP 7.2 (end of life, no fix available)

The following Google Cloud products are impacted:

  • App Engine Standard (second-generation PHP 7.2–8.5 runtimes)
  • App Engine Flexible
  • Cloud Run
  • Cloud Run functions

What should I do?

Patched PHP runtimes are available across App Engine Standard, App Engine Flexible, Cloud Run, and Cloud Run functions. The updated PHP versions include updates against CVE-2026-126714, CVE-2026-115560, and other important security fixes. Take the following action.

  • Immediate mitigation, all PHP applications
    • Disable Session Upload Progress: If your application does not require tracking upload progress, disabling this feature in php.ini mitigates the primary attack path for phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714) in particular: session.upload_progress.enabled = 0
    • Where feasible, switch PHP session storage away from local filesystem handlers (session.save_handler = files) to an external store such as Redis, Memcache, or a database.
  • Self-managed containers
    • Cloud Run containers and App Engine flexible custom runtimes can upgrade immediately to upstream PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, or 8.5.13, rebuild, and redeploy without waiting on Google-managed runtime rollouts.
  • Managed runtimes with automatic base image updates
    • Apply the Disable Session Upload Progress mitigations above
    • App Engine standard (second-generation PHP 8.2–8.5) and Cloud Run services / Cloud Run functions with automatic base image updates enabled receive patched PHP runtimes automatically.
  • Managed runtimes without automatic updates or pinned versions:
    • Apply the Disable Session Upload Progress mitigations above
    • App Engine flexible (managed PHP runtime), Cloud Run jobs and worker pools, Cloud Functions (1st gen), and deployments pinned to a specific patch string must rebuild and redeploy to pick up the updated runtime images.
  • End-of-life PHP versions (7.2–8.1):
    • No upstream patches will be released for PHP 8.1 or earlier. Customers should upgrade to a supported PHP runtime (8.2 or later) or apply the php.ini / non-file session mitigations above.

What vulnerabilities are being addressed?

CVE-2026-126714 is a vulnerability in PHP's default file-based session handler (session.save_handler = files). When PHP writes session data (for example, during unauthenticated file upload progress tracking), the write is not atomic. If a PHP worker stops abruptly mid-write—such as from a memory limit or request timeout—a partially overwritten, malformed session file can remain on disk. When a later request calls session_start(), PHP deserializes that file; with crafted input, an unauthenticated remote attacker can manipulate the deserialized data to execute arbitrary code. Because this issue stems from how session files are written to disk rather than earlier PHP request-cleanup vulnerabilities, upgrading to a patched PHP version or applying the session mitigations above is required.

CVE-2026-115560 is a critical PHP vulnerability where a session serializer mismatch can lead to a remote code execution.

 Critical CVE-2026-126714
CVE-2026-115560

entry.title: GCP-2026-089
entry.content:
Published: 2026-11-20

Description

Description Severity Notes

On November 18, 2026, F5 disclosed HTTP/2 vulnerabilities CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 in NGINX Open Source (1.19.7-1.31.8 for CVE-2026-123633; 1.9.5-1.31.8 for CVE-2026-123007) and NGINX Plus, alongside eight additional NGINX CVEs in F5's master advisory (K000164058). Under specific configuration and traffic conditions, an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash an NGINX worker process (DoS) or potentially achieve remote code execution (RCE). Google Cloud's core load balancing and managed infrastructure (including Google Front End, Cloud Load Balancing, GKE control plane, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, and App Engine) are not affected. This bulletin provides guidance for customers operating self-managed NGINX deployments on Google Cloud.

What should I do?

  • Managed Google Cloud services: No customer action is required if you rely solely on unaffected Google Cloud managed platforms (including Google Front End, Cloud Load Balancing, GKE control plane, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, and App Engine). Google is patching any isolated Google-managed components internally, with zero customer impact and no customer action required.
  • Customer-managed NGINX on Google Cloud (GKE Ingress Controllers, Compute Engine VMs, and NGINX-based Cloud Marketplace images): Google has also temporarily delisted affected Google-maintained Click-to-Deploy NGINX listings on Cloud Marketplace while patched images are being prepared.
    • Patch: Upgrade NGINX Open Source to 1.31.9 (mainline) or 1.30.7 (stable), or NGINX Plus to the latest fixed releases (37.0.7.1 / 37.2.0.1 for CVE-2026-123633; 37.0.8.1 / 37.3.0.1 for CVE-2026-123007) in F5 advisory K000164058 to remediate these vulnerabilities and all November 18 F5 CVEs (see also the Wiz research blog).
    • Temporary mitigation (if unable to patch immediately): Disable HTTP/2 on exposed NGINX listeners (for example, set use-http2: "false" in ingress-nginx or remove http2 listener directives and reload), or place a Google Cloud External Application Load Balancer in front of NGINX configured to speak HTTP/1.1 to backends. (Note: Disabling HTTP/2 does not mitigate non-HTTP/2 CVEs, so upgrading to a patched release remains recommended.)

What vulnerabilities are being addressed?

  • CVE-2026-123633 (NGINX Open Source 1.19.7-1.31.8; NGINX Plus R33+ / 37.0.0-37.2.0.0): Reentrant HTTP/2 connection-draining heap use-after-free in ngx_http_v2_module when reverse proxying (proxy_pass, fastcgi_pass, uwsgi_pass, scgi_pass, or grpc_pass) under worker_connections depletion, enabling worker crash (DoS) or potential remote code execution (if ASLR is disabled or bypassed).
  • CVE-2026-123007 (NGINX Open Source 1.9.5-1.31.8; NGINX Plus R33+ / 37.0.0-37.3.0.0): HTTP/2 flow-control window vulnerability during crafted HTTP/2 traffic processing; does not require reverse proxying and can also affect NGINX serving static content directly over HTTP/2, enabling worker process crashes (DoS) or potential remote code execution (if ASLR is disabled or bypassed).
  • Additional F5 November 18, 2026 CVEs: F5 master advisory K000164058 also discloses eight additional NGINX CVEs alongside these two primary HTTP/2 vulnerabilities; upgrading to a patched release remediates these vulnerabilities and all November 18 F5 CVEs.
 High
  • CVE-2026-123633
  • CVE-2026-123007

entry.title: GCP-2026-088
entry.content:
Published: 2026-11-19

Updated: 2026-11-20

Description

Description Severity Notes

2026-11-20 Update: Added GKE patch versions containing fixes for Container-Optimized OS for minor versions 1.32 and 1.33. Patches for GKE 1.37 on Container-Optimized OS and Ubuntu node images are still in progress.

A denial-of-service vulnerability (CVE-2026-99288) was discovered in the Linux kernel TCP implementation. The flaw can cause a kernel panic (denial of service) on the affected virtual machine; it does not allow privilege escalation or container breakout to code execution on the host. A remote attacker can trigger it by sending specially crafted TCP packets to a reachable TCP listener on a node, Pod, or the cluster control plane's IP-based endpoint. Internal traffic within the same VPC can also trigger this vulnerability.

GKE Standard clusters and GKE Autopilot clusters running Container-Optimized OS or Ubuntu prior to the patched versions are affected across both cluster control planes and worker nodes. Pods running in GKE Sandbox (gVisor) and Windows Server node pools are not affected.

For instructions and more details, see the GKE security bulletin.

 High CVE-2026-99288
